results.quote: Theorem 1.3. For \(t\ge 1\), there exists an m-edge graph G such that every t-thick Steiner shortcut graph G_+ for G either has diameter \(m^{\Omega(1/t)}\) or \(m^{1+\Omega(1/t)}\) edges.

results.previous_best: Hesse's lower bound: either |E_+| \ge |P| or diameter n^{\Omega(1/k)}
results.quote: Theorem 2.2. Let \(k\ge 2\) be an integer, and let \(G=(V,E)\in\mathcal{G}_k\) be an n-vertex, n^{1+O(1/k)}-edge graph with associated critical vertex pairs \(P\subseteq V\times V\). Then G admits a k-thick Steiner shortcut graph \(G_+=(V\cup V_+,E\cup E_+)\) with \(|E_+|=|E|/n^{\Omega(1/k)}\), such that every \((s,t)\in P\) has dist_{G_+}(s,t)=k.

Theorem 3.1. For \(k\ge 2\), \(t\le 0.99k\), and \(m=2^{\omega(k\mathrm{log}k)}\), every t-thick Steiner shortcut for the m-edge graph \(G\in\mathcal{G}_k\) requires either \(m^{\Omega(1/k)}\) diameter or \(m^{1+\Omega(1/k)}\) edges.

Theorem 3.3. For \(k\ge 2\), there are parameters c,d,p such that with probability 1-1/poly(m), every t-thick Steiner shortcut for the m-edge graph \(G\in\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_k(c,d,p)\) requires either diameter \(m^{\Omega(1/k)}\) or \(m^{1+\Omega(1/k)}\) edges, provided that \(1.01t\le\frac{8}{7}k\) and \(m=2^{\omega(k\mathrm{log}k)}\).

Theorem A.1. For every sufficiently small constant \(\epsilon>0\), there exists an infinite family of n-node, m-edge directed graphs G, where \(m\in\left[n,n^{2-4\epsilon^{1/2}+\epsilon}\right]\), such that every Steiner reachability shortcut of G has size at least \(\tilde{\Omega}(m^{1-\epsilon})\) or diameter at least \(\Omega(n^\epsilon)\).

results.previous_best: VXX24 lower bound: any O(m)-size shortcut has diameter \Omega(n^{1/5})
results.quote: Theorem C.3 (Steiner Shortcut for [VXX24] Construction). Graph G and set of paths P admit a Steiner reachability shortcut set H such that 1. H has O(r^4)=O(|V(G)|/r) Steiner nodes and O(r^5)=O(|E(G)|) edges, and 2. For every \(s\rightsquigarrow t\) path \(P\in\mathcal{P}\), there exists an \(s\rightsquigarrow t\) path of length two in \(G\cup H\).
